subject: chemistry
title: Weathering and Erosion
welcome_lead: Wind, water and ice slowly chew rocks into tiny grains. Welcome to weathering.
meta_desc: Learn weathering, erosion and transport in this KS3 chemistry adventure on rocks.
final_note: You can now explain how mountains turn into beaches.

concepts.def: Breaking rock into smaller pieces in place.
Freeze-thaw, plant roots, etc. break rock physically.
Acid rain or water dissolves parts of rock.
Plants and animals break rock down.
Sediment dropping out and settling somewhere new.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical: water gets into cracks, freezes, expands and splits the rock.
Chemical: acid rain reacts with minerals in the rock.
Biological: tree roots push cracks apart; lichens release acids.

Once a rock is broken into pieces, erosion carries them away. Wind, rivers, waves and glaciers all move sediment.

Weathering breaks. Erosion moves.
Eventually moving water or wind slows down and drops the sediment. This is deposition. Over millions of years, deposited layers can become sedimentary rock — and the cycle continues.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
options: They are the same
Weathering breaks rocks, erosion moves the pieces
Erosion only happens in deserts
Weathering happens only underwater

mcqs.q: Freeze-thaw cracking is an example of:
options: Chemical weathering
Physical weathering
Biological weathering
Deposition

mcqs.q: When an acid neutralises an alkali, what is the pH of the resulting solution?
options: Neutralisation always produces a solution with pH 0.
Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
Neutralisation always produces a solution with pH exactly 7 regardless of the acid and base used.
Approximately 7 if equivalent amounts of strong acid and strong alkali react — but it varies with strength.

mcqs.q: Why is the 4s orbital filled before the 3d orbital?
options: Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
The order of reaction is always equal to the number of reactants in the equation.
Because the 4s orbital has a lower energy than 3d when both are empty, so electrons fill it first.
Because the 4s shell is closer to the nucleus than the 3d shell.
